### Part A

<details><summary>**2.** An example README _(click to expand)_</summary>

````markdown
# RNA-seq analysis of _Culex pipiens_

- Author: Jelmer Poelstra
- Date: 2026-10-23
- GitHub repository: TBA
- This was run at the Pitzer cluster of the Ohio Supercomputer Center (<www.osc.edu>)
- OSC working dir: /fs/ess/PAS3493/people/jelmer/week10/exercises

## Prerequisites

- **Input files**:
  - The input files are:
    - Paired-end FASTQ files
    - Reference genomes files (assembly and annotation)

- **Software**:
  - The scripts will run programs using Singularity/Apptainer containers
    available online, with links contained inside the scripts
  - If running at OSC, no software installations are needed
  - If you're not at OSC, you need to have `apptainer` and `Slurm` installed.

- You don't need to create the output dirs because the scripts will do so.

## Set up: Set file paths

```bash
# Inputs:
fastq_dir=garrigos/fastq
ref_assembly=garrigos/ref/GCF_016801865.2_TS_CPP_V2_genomic.fna
ref_annotation=garrigos/ref/annot.gtf

# Base output dir:
outdir=results
```
````

### Part B

<details><summary>**4.** Run the FastQC script for all FASTQ files _(click to expand)_</summary>

- Code to submit the batch jobs:

  ```bash
  for fastq in "$fastq_dir"/*fastq.gz; do
      sbatch scripts/fastqc.sh "$fastq" "$outdir"/fastqc
  done
  ```

- Monitor the jobs:
  1. `squeue -u $USER -l` until all jobs are out of the list i.e. are done
  2. `less slurm-fastqc*` to read over at least one Slurm log file
  3. Check your email and/or run `tail slurm-fastqc*` to make sure no job has failed
  4. Check the main output files with `ls -lh results/fastqc`

- NOTE: The code to run the above steps does not need to be stored in your README,
  as this is the kind of code you repeatedly run and which does not produce results.
  You're best off typing this directly in the terminal.

- Move the Slurm log files with `mv -v slurm-fastqc* results/fastqc/logs/`.
  **It can be good to store this line in your README.**

</details>

## The code of the shell scripts

<details><summary>Click to see the code of the `fastqc.sh` script</summary>
```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=PAS3493
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mail-type=FAIL
#SBATCH --output=slurm-fastqc-%j.out
set -euo pipefail

# Load the OSC module for FastQC
module load fastqc/0.12.1

# Copy the placeholder variables
fastq="$1"
outdir="$2"

# Initial logging
echo "# Starting script fastqc.sh"
date
echo "# Input FASTQ file:   $fastq"
echo "# Output dir:         $outdir"
echo

# Create the output dir (with a subdir for Slurm logs)
mkdir -p "$outdir"/logs

# Run FastQC
fastqc \
    --threads 4 \
    --outdir "$outdir" \
    "$fastq"

# Final logging
echo
echo "# Used FastQC version:"
fastqc --version
echo
echo "# Successfully finished script fastqc.sh"
date
```
</details>

<details><summary>Click to see the code of the `multiqc.sh` script</summary>
```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=PAS3493
#SBATCH --mail-type=FAIL
#SBATCH --output=slurm-multiqc-%j.out
set -euo pipefail

# Constants
MULTIQC_CONTAINER=oras://community.wave.seqera.io/library/multiqc:1.31--e111a2e953475c51

# Copy the placeholder variables
indir="$1"
outdir="$2"

# Initial logging
echo "# Starting script multiqc.sh"
date
echo "# Input dir:                      $indir"
echo "# Output file:                    $outdir"
echo

# Create the output dir (with a subdir for Slurm logs)
mkdir -p "$outdir"/logs

# Run MultiQC
apptainer exec "$MULTIQC_CONTAINER" multiqc \
    --outdir "$outdir" \
    "$indir"

# Final logging
echo
echo "# Used MultiQC version:"
apptainer exec "$MULTIQC_CONTAINER" multiqc --version
echo "# Successfully finished script multiqc.sh"
date
```
</details>

<details><summary>Click to see the code of the `trimgalore.sh` script</summary>
```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=PAS3493
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --time=30
#SBATCH --output=slurm-trimgalore-%j.out
#SBATCH --mail-type=FAIL
set -euo pipefail

# Constants
TRIMGALORE_CONTAINER=oras://community.wave.seqera.io/library/trim-galore:2.3.0--a56e49e832976df4

# Copy the placeholder variables
R1="$1"
R2="$2"
outdir="$3"

# Initial logging
echo "# Starting script trimgalore.sh"
date
echo "# Input R1 FASTQ file:      $R1"
echo "# Input R2 FASTQ file:      $R2"
echo "# Output dir:               $outdir"
echo

# Create the output dir (with a subdir for Slurm logs)
mkdir -p "$outdir"/logs

# Run TrimGalore
apptainer exec "$TRIMGALORE_CONTAINER" trim_galore \
    --2colour 20 \
    --cores 8 \
    --paired \
    --fastqc \
    --output_dir "$outdir" \
    "$R1" \
    "$R2"

# Build the output file names:
sample_id=$(basename "$R1" _R1.fastq.gz)
R1_out_init="$outdir"/"$sample_id"_R1_val_1.fq.gz
R2_out_init="$outdir"/"$sample_id"_R2_val_2.fq.gz
R1_out_final="$outdir"/"$sample_id"_R1.fastq.gz
R2_out_final="$outdir"/"$sample_id"_R2.fastq.gz

# Rename the output files:
echo
echo "# Renaming the output files:"
mv -v "$R1_out_init" "$R1_out_final"
mv -v "$R2_out_init" "$R2_out_final"

# Final logging
echo
echo "# TrimGalore version:"
apptainer exec "$TRIMGALORE_CONTAINER" trim_galore -v
echo "# Successfully finished script trimgalore.sh"
date
```
</details>

<details><summary>Click to see the code of the `salmon_index.sh` script</summary>
```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=PAS3493
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --time=60
#SBATCH --mail-type=FAIL
#SBATCH --output=slurm-salmon_index-%j.out
set -euo pipefail

# Constants
SALMON_CONTAINER=<???>

# Copy the placeholder variables
transcripts="$1"
outdir="$2"

# Initial logging
echo "# Starting script salmon_index.sh"
date
echo "# Input transcriptome FASTA file: $transcripts"
echo "# Output dir:                     $outdir"
echo

# Create the output dir (with a subdir for Slurm logs)
mkdir -p "$outdir"/logs

# Run Salmon
apptainer exec "$SALMON_CONTAINER" salmon index \
    --transcripts "$transcripts" \
    --index "$outdir" \
    --threads 8

#? - Note: This command was kept as simple as possible - if using Salmon in your research,
#?   look into a "decoy-aware" index, which adds the genome sequence as "decoys"
#?   (see https://salmon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/salmon.html#preparing-transcriptome-indices-mapping-based-mode)
#? - Explanation of some of the options used:
#?   --transcripts  => The transcriptome FASTA file (can be gzipped)
#?   --index        => The output dir for the index

# Final logging
echo
echo "# Used Salmon version:"
apptainer exec "$SALMON_CONTAINER" salmon --version
echo "# Successfully finished script salmon_index.sh"
date
```
</details>

<details><summary>Click to see the code of the `salmon_quant.sh` script</summary>
```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=PAS3493
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --time=30
#SBATCH --mail-type=FAIL
#SBATCH --output=slurm-salmon_quant-%j.out
set -euo pipefail

# Constants
SALMON_CONTAINER=<???>

# Copy the placeholder variables
R1="$1"
R2="$2"
index_dir="$3"
outdir="$4"

# Infer the "sample ID" - we need this for the output dir specification
sample_id=$(basename "$R1" _R1.fastq.gz)

# Initial logging
echo "# Starting script salmon_quant.sh"
date
echo "# Input R1 FASTQ file:            $R1"
echo "# Input R2 FASTQ file:            $R2"
echo "# Input Salmon index:             $index_dir"
echo "# Output dir:                     $outdir"
echo "# Sample ID (inferred):           $sample_id"
echo

# Create the output dir (with a subdir for Slurm logs)
mkdir -p "$outdir"/logs

# Run Salmon
apptainer exec "$SALMON_CONTAINER" salmon quant \
    --index "$index_dir" \
    --libType A \
    --mates1 "$R1" \
    --mates2 "$R2" \
    --threads 8 \
    --output "$outdir"/"$sample_id"

#? - Note: keeping this command as simple as possible -
#?   if using Salmon in your research, then look into, e.g., the --gcBias and
#?   --seqBias options as well.
#? - Explanation of some of the options used:
#?   --libType A                     => Automatically infer the library type (e.g., strandedness)
#?   --mates1 / --mates2             => The R1 and R2 FASTQ files of a paired-end sample
#?   --output "$outdir"/"$sample_id" => Each sample gets its own output dir

# Final logging
echo
echo "# Used Salmon version:"
apptainer exec "$SALMON_CONTAINER" salmon --version
echo "# Successfully finished script salmon_quant.sh"
date
```
</details>
